# `operation-removed`

Operation removed without enough deprecation

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `operation-removed` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Paths and operations ([RULES.md section 2](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An operation in the base no longer exists in the revision, and no operation with the same `operationId` replaced it at another path.

## Why this default

Clients that call it get 404 or 405 responses.

## Example

From test case [`operation-removed`](../../test/cases/operation-removed/): Removing an operation is an error.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          '200':
            description: ok
-   '/pets/{id}':
-     delete:
-       responses:
-         '200':
-           description: ok
```

Findings:

- `operation-removed` · error · DELETE /pets/{id}

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `unless.deprecated-for-days` | `90` | Allow removal (as `operation-removed-after-deprecation`) once the operation has been deprecated this long. Can be set per stability level. |
| `unless.past-sunset` | `true` | Allow removal once the operation's sunset date has passed. |

```yaml
rules:
  operation-removed: error
```

## How to fix

Mark the operation `deprecated` first and remove it after the deprecation period, or keep it and point clients at the replacement.
